title: Slow Roast Pork Belly
subtitle: Crisp crackling and tender meat from a long, slow roast
excerpt: Pork belly rewards patience. A long time at a low temperature renders the fat and makes the meat spoon-tender. A blast of high heat at the end crisps the skin. The apple roasts alongside and needs no extra work.
sourceNotes: Slow-roasted pork belly has been a British pub and restaurant staple since the late 1990s when cheaper cuts were rediscovered by chefs. The technique of rendering at low heat then finishing at high to crisp the skin was popularised by British food writers in that era.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cooked pork belly freezes well. Slice before freezing. Reheat from frozen at 200C for 15 minutes to re-crisp.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Score and season the skin the day before, refrigerate uncovered. Dry skin makes better crackling.
recipe.temperatureNote: Start at 160C Fan 140C / Gas 3. Finish at 240C Fan 220C / Gas 9 to crisp the skin.

content.text: The skin must be very dry before going into the oven. Pat it with kitchen paper and, if time allows, leave it uncovered in the fridge overnight.

items.prepNote: skin scored in close parallel lines

content.text: Pat the pork skin completely dry with kitchen paper.
Rub the skin with olive oil and plenty of salt, working it into the scored lines.
Scatter the garlic, rosemary, and fennel seeds in the roasting tin. Lay the pork on top, skin side up.
Roast at 160C for 2 hours and 30 minutes.
Add the apple halves to the tin, cut side down, for the last 30 minutes.
After 3 hours total, check the internal temperature. It should read at least 75C.
Turn the oven up to 240C. Roast for a further 15 to 20 minutes to crisp the skin.
Rest uncovered for 20 minutes before carving.

items.symptom: Skin blistered but did not crunch.
items.cause: Skin was damp or not scored deeply enough.
items.fix: Dry more thoroughly. Score deeper, all the way through the rind.

items.cause: Not cooked long enough at low temperature.
items.fix: Return to 160C and roast for another 30 minutes.

items.cause: Oven too hot or skin too close to the top element.
items.fix: Lower to 220C and watch closely. Move rack down one level.
